rhetorical_skeleton.writing_objective: Justifying the integration of two distinct technologies (AAV + IRS) as a 'New Paradigm' for 6G.
key_components: Context setting (6G requirements: eMBB, URLLC, mMTC)
Complementary Analysis: How IRS fixes AAV constraints (Energy/Reliability) and vice versa
Visual Structure Diagram (Fig. 2) acting as a navigation map

rhetorical_skeleton.writing_objective: Grounding the technology in standard industry verticals to prove relevance.
key_components: Mapping scenarios to 6G verticals: SAGIN (eMBB), V2X (URLLC), IoT (mMTC)
Derivation of Key Issues (Energy, Security, Enhanced Comms) from these scenarios

rhetorical_skeleton.writing_objective: Establishing technical credibility by reviewing actual implementations before theoretical solutions.
key_components: Technology Enablers: Channel Estimation, Beamforming, Resource Allocation, Trajectory Opt

rhetorical_skeleton.writing_objective: Systematic review of literature with explicit synthesis of takeaways.
key_components: Categorization by Key Issue (from Section II)
Solution Summary Tables (Table III) with technology columns
Explicit 'Lesson X' paragraphs summarizing insights at the end of subsections

visual_roadmap.layout_logic: Uses a 'Structure Tree' (Fig. 2) early to guide the reader through the complex hierarchy. Dedicates a full schematic figure to EACH major application scenario (Fig 3, 4, 5) to visualize the 'Why'.
required_table_types: Survey Comparison Table with 'Scope' columns (Table I)
Solution Summary Tables (Table III) categorizing Ref, Technologies (Channel Est, Beamforming, etc.), and Objectives

writing_style_secrets.phrasing_patterns: Uses explicit bolded 'Lesson X:' paragraphs to enforce synthesis. This turns a literature review into a tutorial.
writing_style_secrets.technical_depth_management: Bridges the gap between theory and practice by dedicating a specific section to 'Prototypes' (Hardware/Software) before discussing algorithms.

top_3_tips: The 'Verticals' Anchor: Align your application scenarios with standard network definitions (eMBB, URLLC, mMTC). It makes your classification feel standard and exhaustive.
Explicit Lessons: Don't just summarize papers. Add a bold 'Lesson' paragraph at the end of each subsection to tell the reader *what it means*.
The Prototype Bridge: If your survey is theoretical, adding a section on 'Prototypes/Hardware' significantly boosts credibility by showing you understand the physical constraints.
mistakes_to_avoid: Ignoring the Physical Layer: Discussing algorithms (Beamforming) without mentioning the hardware constraints (Power consumption, Prototypes).
Generic Scenario Descriptions: Visualizing scenarios without specific network architecture details (BS, IRS, Users, Links).
